title: a run button on phone and laptop, seamless walk-to-run, in both venues
lensAText: a sceptical mobile game UX lead and animator. Look at the builder's frames with the Read tool, then build dist/artifact.html yourself and take your own frames in ONE short Playwright script: in Lot 57 and Stoppage Time (Go To, Get out) at 390x844 (phone viewport copy, isMobile, hasTouch, DPR 3) and 1280x720: is the RUN button easy to find and reach with the left thumb, sleek and high-tech, never covering the look area or other buttons; does holding it (and Shift on the laptop) run, does the lock work, does the walk blend into the run with no pop or stutter in first and third person, do collisions, crowds, stairs and tap-to-go still behave? Judge the look against the driving touch controls' style.
brief: THE OWNER (2026-11-12 ~5:20 AM PT): "lets make a running button for both the laptop and phone so it should be seamless". TODAY (read src/onfoot/lot57/input.ts and player.ts, and the sports bar's own venues/sportsbar/player.ts and main.ts): on foot the player walks at 1.4 m/s and jogs at 3.0 m/s, only outdoors (player.ts: 'run && !this.indoors'); jog is reached by Shift on a keyboard or by pushing the touch stick past 92 %; there is NO visible run control, so players don't know running exists. BUILD, in Lot 57 and Stoppage Time, both inside the game (src/onfoot/embed.ts mount) and on the standalone pages: (1) A visible RUN button. Phone: a big, sleek, high-tech thumb button just above or beside where the left stick floats (in the same visual language as the driving touch controls: dark glass, bold label, accent edge, pressed state), reachable while the left thumb steers; hold to run, plus a double-tap to lock running on and a tap to release; it never blocks the look area or the action buttons. Laptop: the same button on screen (clickable) AND Shift held to run, with Caps Lock or a key toggle as a lock if cheap; show the hint 'Shift to run' once in the existing hint chip. Gamepad: left-stick click (L3) toggles run. (2) Seamless: walk to run and back with smooth acceleration (about 0.3 s up, 0.2 s down), the walk cycle blending into the existing jog/run gait the people builder already has (the NPC jogger uses it) with no pop, a slight camera bob and FOV ease in first person, the third-person camera keeping up without lag; stopping is crisp. A real run speed (about 4.5 m/s outdoors); indoors a gentler run (about 2.6 m/s) instead of none, and no running through crowds (slow to walk near people and on stairs); the existing collision, pathing (tap to go stays walking) and occlusion keep working. (3) Honest and cheap: no stamina system unless trivial (none is required); no per-frame allocation; phone-cheap; reduced motion: no bob or FOV change. Do NOT edit src/onfoot/people/* (another lane rebuilds the characters there; use the gait the builder already exposes; if a parameter you need is missing, say so instead), src/preview/hands*, spec.ts, car-wheel.ts or Physics.ts. ADD regression checks (both venues: the RUN button exists on phone and laptop layouts, holding it or Shift raises the speed to the run speed outdoors and the indoor run speed indoors, releasing returns to walk within 0.3 s, the lock toggles, the gait switches without a frame where the mesh pops). PROVE: npx tsc --noEmit; npm run build (one owner-test mark); npm test -- --only=boot,venues and the new checks; the standalone venue builds (npx vite build --config src/onfoot/vite.config.ts and --config src/onfoot/vite.sportsbar.config.ts); frames: the phone layout (390x844 phone viewport copy, DPR 3) and laptop (1280x720) with the RUN button idle and pressed, in both venues, plus a 6-frame strip of the walk-to-run transition in third person. Log it in PROJECT_OC_PROGRESS.md and the venues' own docs.
